answer: An identity is only an anchor once its stake is slashable and it has survived a slow challenge window—a glacier-paced cooldown that makes mass fake registrations expensive in capital and time. Sybil resistance here uses a bonded-reputation checkpoint: each agent must lock a stake and pass one liveness attestation before its identity is counted. Reaching voting summit requires cumulative peer attestations, so an attacker must fund thousands of distinct bonded identities, wait out each cooldown, and risk total slashing. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
